description: Canonical reverse-coverage registry for testable normative clauses. Each row pins one protocol obligation to a stable clause_id, an exact prose anchor, a digest of that section's current text, and the evidence that proves it. It closes the direction vector-registry.json cannot: from prose obligation to executable proof. See spec/v1/zh/conformance/conformance-suite.md section 2.

coverage_scope.rule: This registry covers the high-risk observable obligation set named in included_categories. It is deliberately not a numbering of every normative sentence under spec/v1/zh; mechanically numbering prose would manufacture meaningless MUSTs. A green release gate proves that every registered clause has live evidence and that no registered section changed without review. It does NOT prove that every MUST in the specification is registered.
coverage_scope.extension_rule: Adding or changing a high-risk observable obligation that this registry is intended to evidence requires adding or updating a clause in the same change. Obligations without executable evidence stay explicitly outside this registry rather than pointing at unrelated evidence. Because section_digest pins registered anchors, editing a registered section fails the release gate until its existing clause and evidence are re-reviewed; this rule does not imply exhaustive coverage of every normative sentence in an included category.
coverage_scope.executable_fixture_rule: A clause in one of executable_fixture_categories with testability_grade=vector MUST name vectors that are carried by a fixture declaring a security_evidence entry for them, and that entry MUST map every decision point of the obligation onto resolvable evidence inside the fixture. This is the successor to the deleted aggregate security-closure fixture: the obligation set is whatever is registered here, never a list inside a lint. The remaining categories are outside the rule today because clauses in them still name vectors with no fixture carrier; widening the list is how that gap gets closed, and narrowing it to keep a clause green is not.
coverage_scope.executable_evidence_exemption_rule: Every (clause_id, vector_id) pair inside executable_fixture_categories that does not yet have executable evidence MUST be enumerated here with its reason. The list only shrinks: once a vector gains a security_evidence carrier its row MUST be removed, and the gate fails while a stale row remains. A pair that is neither evidenced nor enumerated fails the gate, so the open gap stays visible in the canonical registry instead of inside a lint.

registry_rules: clause_id values are stable and MUST NOT be reused after a clause is closed; retire a clause by setting status=inactive instead of deleting the row.
source_anchor MUST be a repository-relative markdown path plus an existing heading slug. section_digest MUST equal the sha256 of that heading's section text as computed by tools/artifact_lint.

testability_grade=vector rows MUST list evidence_refs containing active vector ids from vector-registry.json. testability_grade=api_shape or audit rows MUST instead declare test_plan describing the non-vector proof.
A clause MUST NOT claim evidence it does not have: an obligation with no executable proof stays out of this registry rather than pointing at an unrelated vector.

A clause whose category is listed in coverage_scope.executable_fixture_categories MUST have executable fixture evidence for each of its evidence_refs. Adding such a clause without the fixture entry, or deleting the fixture entry, turns the security evidence gate red.

clauses.requirement: Canonical JSON serialization (key order, number form, NFC strings, duplicate-key rejection) is the single encoding used for every digest, signature and canonical comparison.
Digest suite identifiers, canonical event digest computation and the bytewise tie-break order are fixed; implementations MUST NOT substitute another hash encoding or comparison direction.

The signature carrier MUST cryptographically protect its algorithm selection, and the binding payload MUST bind domain and audience; a signature valid for one algorithm, domain or audience MUST NOT verify for another. Section 6.0.2 fixes one construction for every registered proof context: the unsigned projection deletes the proof carrier member rather than nulling it and never defaults an absent optional, an absent optional binding field is omitted rather than written as null, audience is a single string or a duplicate-free array with the single-value form mandatory for one audience, and the context constant is a binding object member rather than a JWS header parameter, so a signature valid under one object family's context MUST NOT verify for another.

HLC well-formedness, logical-counter overflow handling and the causal-first usage boundary: HLC breaks ties between causally incomparable items only and MUST NOT select a winner in shared protocol state.
Cursors are opaque server-issued tokens bound to their query scope; clients MUST NOT parse or forge them and cross-scope replay MUST be rejected.
Encrypted envelopes carry a pre-encryption immutable header; AAD digest and ciphertext digest are computed over fixed transcripts and any mismatch MUST fail closed.
Transport encoding bounds: Content-Encoding is forbidden on non-streaming JSON operations and every size limit MUST be enforced before the body is fully buffered or parsed.
Every operation_id ends with <kind>.<action> drawn from the closed kind set, and the action MUST describe a protocol effect rather than an HTTP method name.
clauses.test_plan: Enforced mechanically by tools/artifact_lint: every operation_id in operation-registry.json is checked against the closed kind set and against forbidden HTTP-method action names. There is no runtime vector because the obligation is on the published contract, not on request handling.

clauses.requirement: Every write operation declares a machine-readable idempotency mechanism and retry safety; clients MUST NOT be left to guess the recovery path of an uncertain outcome.
Protected current-v1 endpoints require sender-constrained proof of possession; a bare bearer session grant MUST NOT authenticate a protected request.

An accepted ak.mls.genesis activates its effective scope irreversibly: no later Event, downgrade or group replacement returns that scope to plaintext, and a plaintext write after activation is rejected rather than silently accepted or re-encrypted. Encrypted prepare and authority-forward submit into a definitely inactive scope return generic failed_precondition without a durable write; a temporarily unreadable current MLS result returns temporarily_unavailable. Every encrypted envelope is the closed {version, content_type, encryption_context, ciphertext} with encryption_context limited to epoch, group_state_ref and registered routing context; the receiver reconstructs the exact closed pre-encryption header from the outer signed Event, the effective scope, the Event kind, its own verified current public group result and the sender leaf, and MUST NOT trust any copy carried alongside the envelope. Any AAD, ciphertext-digest or encryption_context mismatch fails closed with no partial write, no plaintext downgrade and no retry under different secrets.

Directory v1 is read-only and exposes only closed public Realm metadata through describe, search and exact resolve. It registers no announce, withdraw, ingest proof or governance-authority surface; hidden, expired and unknown Realm locators remain indistinguishable, and no query result is authorization evidence.

For ordinary grant/root lineage (the dedicated owned_agent terminal source has its own registered contract): A grant stays within the union of the authorities its issuer_authority_refs name and within their per-action validity window. A grant without ordinary authority_control cannot be a grant ref; a ref with authority_regrant_allowed=false can issue only an explicitly terminal max_authority_depth=0 child. A grant ref supplies issuer authority only when its concrete subject ActorId equals the child issuer ActorId in full; cycles, inactive refs and same-DID cross-Station replay MUST fail closed rather than widen the effective permission set. A first-issued grant whose ancestor no longer authorizes uses failed_precondition with grant_exceeds_issuer_authority; other security operations use capability_denied without disclosing inaccessible ancestor state. A realm_root ref is valid only while the authority-root typed current result's current authority_generation still equals the generation the ref carries, read under the registered inclusion proof at a RealmCommit basis; that delegation generation advances only on ak.realm.authority.reset and MUST NOT be conflated with the governing Station tenure governance_generation, so a planned Station handoff MUST NOT invalidate any grant and a controller transfer MUST leave every child grant valid.

Field patches apply atomically against the declared pre-state; a partially applied patch or an unbound pre-state MUST be rejected. $op="unset" MUST NOT remove a registered redactable content-carrier slot, while $op="set" on the same slot and $op="unset" on metadata paths MUST be accepted. A patch path MUST NOT address a reducer-managed field of the target object kind; the per-object forbidden set, its universal minimum set and its one named View state exemption are read from registry/reducer-managed-path-registry.json, never re-derived from prose.

Call state transitions follow the registered matrix, terminal states are absorbing, exact Event replay is a no-op, and competing commands against one revision produce one confirmed successor plus durable stale rejection outcomes. Compact media bindings carry only expires_at/issuer_kid/sig; rebuild the signed seven-tuple from the exact enclosing Event/Call and roster entry, require its frozen focus to match the accepted selection on write, and never reinterpret old signatures using a later focus. v1 rejects every mute_override write, including a mixed delta, because the retained call-only selector cannot represent independent legs; ordinary call and self-mute paths remain available.

Account Data keys are server-versioned compare-and-set registers with explicitly registered writer authority and holder self operations: a stale write MUST fail with cas_conflict, the revision high-water mark never goes backwards, and domain merge runs client-side on plaintext.

Recipient-private delivery preserves exact DeviceMessageEnvelope and MlsWelcomeDelivery branches in one ordered queue: each kind uses its closed durable deduplication key, unacknowledged items survive content expiry and capacity pressure, full capacity rejects new first admission atomically while a Welcome a member Station stores through committed replication counts toward capacity without being refused, and queue removal happens only after explicit cumulative ACK of durably processed items by the same authenticated endpoint.
Optional nullable fields normalize absent and null unless a conditional branch requires the field or x-arkret-presence-semantics=distinct explicitly assigns three business states.
clauses.test_plan: tools/gen_property_presence_manifest.py must classify every tristate audit target with zero unresolved dispositions; the Rust SDK draft202012_runtime and Circle payload tests pin the sole distinct target and its Missing/Null/Value round-trip.

clauses.requirement: The pointer-level closure seeded by the Event envelope root and every registered payload pointer is the jurisdiction of the event_digest preimage rule; following a document-root $ref MUST NOT pull in unreferenced $defs siblings. Every Event-identity candidate in that closure MUST carry one closed x-arkret-preimage-commitment declaration, and prose wording MUST NOT select the verdict. self_identity and same_unit_sibling have no fixed point and MUST NOT be exempted. later_submission is constructible only when preimage-identity-exemption-registry.json carries the exact active row, including the holder-authored Agent draft source-pending forward declaration; non-Event objects outside the closure need no §3.1 exemption.

A cross-object ak.redaction whose target_ref uses the ak:event: form only trims that Event's fields per preserve[] and MUST NOT change any object's state, including the event-derived object minted from a targeted create Event; an object enters state=redacted only through the object typed-id form of target_ref (Message still goes exclusively through ak.message.redact). The two spellings of one 33-octet token land in two distinct object_redaction typed results that are independent and never merge; a reducer MUST NOT canonicalize the ak:event: spelling into the derived object typed id.

Recovery preserves the durable single-writer fence, frozen exact candidate body, unique lineage, original command outcomes and outbox. Competing security commands execute with revision preconditions; rejected commands have no business effects. Timeouts cannot erase a signed position or authorize a parallel lineage. Atomic acceptance never crosses one authority stream, even when streams share a governance Station or serializable store; cross-stream workflows use exact committed references, idempotent saga steps and explicit compensating Events.
clauses.test_plan: Inject restart, lease expiry and old-worker revival, stale basis, old Ack authority rotation, bounded backlog and damaged individual records. Check durable outcomes and progress of independently authorized work. Exercise a cross-stream saga whose successor is temporarily unavailable: the committed predecessor remains committed, exact retry is idempotent, and terminal cancellation is a separately committed compensating Event; no shared store may turn the workflow into a multi-stream atomic write.

clauses.requirement: Forbidden-wire contexts and matchers are registered and resolved before matching; root fields do not apply to arbitrary descendants or another owning schema. Message.track_name is forbidden while the message-create signed payload retains it.
clauses.test_plan: Run vocabulary mutation gates plus shared SDK and cotest scanner positives and negatives covering Message versus Event payload, real create object wrappers, nested KDF pointers, literal aggregate matchers and patch descendants.

clauses.requirement: Any equivalent Bound endorsement accepted by the Realm confirmed sequence can establish ordinary participant authority; the display representative is not an authority head. Distinct binding semantics, wrong Strand and missing confirmation fail closed. The current governance Station performs ordinary admission from authenticated Contact intervals and committed revocations; the origin Station need not be online, while a non-authority receiver can only queue or forward. Founding evidence never becomes an ordinary origin co-signature requirement. Clients consume exact Event plus RealmCommit results without replaying governance history. The current gate follows the immutable founding authorization basis: accepted_contact requires current directional Contact grants; agent_controller requires the exact current controller-owned active Agent and accepted runtime key, without a Contact grant. Runtime key replacement does not rewrite founding or binding identity.
clauses.test_plan: Run Direct Conversation authority and capability-ref tests with one, repeated and concurrent equivalent endorsements, missing confirmation, foreign participants and wrong Strand. Execute bidirectional encrypted messages with origin offline and the current governance Station online; verify each accepted Event has one covering RealmCommit and non-authority receivers only queue or forward. Repeat with the governance Station unavailable and require no shared accepted effect. Known Contact revocation and reload must preserve committed history while blocking later admission; delayed responses cannot reinstall old context. Schema fixtures reject found without binding_event_ref. Exercise owned-Agent bootstrap Message and Add admission without Contact, paused Agent rejection, controller/Station mismatch rejection, and current-key replacement under the same founding basis.

clauses.requirement: Only the exact founder uses registered provisional message authority before peer durable Welcome, with accepted Genesis and current gates. First accepted Bound permanently exits bootstrap; equivalent later endorsements cannot reactivate it. Completion requires the currently occupied peer leaf creation Add and its own durable consume; Remove/re-add cannot inherit an obsolete receipt. Terminal first claims repair in the same group while preserving the immutable initial exact-pair ref.
clauses.test_plan: Run registered provisional-source policy tests; block exact private Realm claim at epoch 0 and consume after Add, then verify real submitted message epoch, peer since_join boundary and eventual convergence. Test post-Bound rejection of bootstrap authority and equivalent endorsement accumulation. Run terminal_founding_claim_repairs_the_same_group_and_keeps_the_first_binding_ref with terminal/pending/durable read cuts, fresh Remove/Add, rejected current-ref substitution and old consumed leaf receipt isolation; verify the four closed resolver admission states and original aa-runtime live repair. The same-Commit Remove is ordered after Add on the wire, and must retire only the before-state leaf. Contact peer endpoint source/reload/glare is additionally checked in Cotest direct_conversation_founding_live and the closed schema fixture.

clauses.requirement: Contact glare requests are exactly two distinct typed EventId wire strings in strict UTF-8 unsigned-byte lexical order, with receipt digests excluded as keys and tiebreakers. Receiving verifiers reject reversed or duplicate refs without normalization before deriving the round ID or founder. Participant ordering separately uses full ActorId RFC 8785 JCS bytes.
clauses.test_plan: Run tools/check_contact_round_kat.py and the SDK Contact round KAT against the same wire-order, digest-order and object-order distinction, reversed input and duplicate refs with equal or different receipt digests. Verify source construction and receiving admission use the same SDK comparison. These checks cover ordering, not a complete two-Station glare flow.

clauses.requirement: Ordinary clients bootstrap from an independently selected Station origin, fetch public describe without credentials or redirects, and durably compare identity and authentication bindings before authentication or credential reuse. Changes require explicit re-enrollment and fresh authentication; client DID-history replay is not required and independent server verification remains mandatory.
clauses.test_plan: Run SDK models-discovery station_connection cases for selected/preconfigured identity, split authority, issuer replacement, inert changes and invalid routes; run http-client public bootstrap redirect/encoding/size negatives. Run Inkson durable store restart, concurrent installation, corruption and explicit replacement cases, OIDC issuer tests and native/wasm compilation. Audit connection and callback gating, frozen authentication context and credential disposal at explicit re-enrollment. These focused checks do not prove a complete live cross-Station deployment or browser authentication flow.

clauses.requirement: supported_profiles is the sole complete-profile self-declaration. verified_profiles ids are unique and contained in supported_profiles, with independently verified evidence. Both calendar profiles require nonempty executable registered TZDB releases.
clauses.test_plan: Run tools.test_residual_simplification and full schema fixtures for both calendar profiles, supported/verified advertisements, missing/empty/unknown TZDB, forbidden claimed_profiles and verified subset violations. This is schema and reference semantic evidence, not a live profile activation or calendar execution test.

clauses.requirement: Self signer keys omit actor/method mirrors, retain complete selector association and invocation context, require historical committed_event_ref plus an independent committed authorization_ref/current revision/governance generation, and leave Signal standalone identity and peer portable evidence intact. Ordinary human current results contain only public_key_b64u after own-Station exact-device directory verification; PCR coordinates remain private and key-only cannot cross into Agent/history.
clauses.test_plan: Run tools.test_self_signer_result_schema and tools.test_residual_simplification for closed query keys, mandatory authorization, historical separation, reordered/unavailable results, duplicate/missing selectors, different methods/Events and invocation mismatch. Runtime authorization, producer signatures and Signal gates remain required and tracked by the existing owner. Run current-signer-contact-endpoint-fixture.json schema cases and Cotest signer_keys_query_live against rebuilt two-Station binaries.

clauses.requirement: Last-resort expiry bounds new distribution only, not historical Welcome decryption with the matching compromised key. Future confidentiality recovery requires effective unknown secret updates and the MLS threat conditions; old plaintext is not made confidential again.
clauses.test_plan: Run tools.test_residual_simplification with keypackage-lifecycle-fixture expiry_security_case for deterministic HPKE GroupSecrets decryption after expiry and failure under an independent fresh key. Synthetic encrypted_group_info context means this is not a full MLS/Station test. The lifecycle vector separately requires product-runner rejection of new expired claims and real group self-updates without retrospective secrecy claims.

clauses.requirement: Every Contact Event carrier authenticates the exact historical producer method and Ed25519 key through the original confirmed source receipt or lineage, then verifies the original holder signature. The first carrier needs no prior relationship or private PCR disclosure. The projection is bound to one Event and cannot authorize another Event or generic Control action. Source acceptance time is fixed at the real slot confirmation, with immutable retries and the matching historical source key. The structurally defined delegated producer branch remains unavailable to v1 Contact commands; human/runtime forbid it. The source freezes a verified complete Agent public locator and the receiver independently verifies its native identity, exact Actor/controller/Station and create-locked binding. This locator grants no authority.
clauses.test_plan: Run check_contact_round_kat.py for source-signed producer descriptors, complete receipt digests, derived normal/glare rounds, absence commitments and key/method mutation rejection. Run SDK Contact carrier cases for the original producer proof, full Account/Agent/controller/source binding and exclusion of generic Control reuse. Run Soland PostgreSQL completion, slot timestamp and historical-key recovery tests plus Inkson exact-request restart tests. The reference vectors alone do not establish a live first-contact exchange or ordinary messaging through a disconnected origin; those require the existing cross-project owner acceptance. Include the three direct/delegated producer contexts and all five carrier conditional schemas, missing/extra/null/core-only/wrong-Agent locators and altered source-signed locator bytes. V1 production acceptance must reject controller-device Agent Contact commands before reservation or Event admission, while ordinary human and Agent-runtime Contact paths remain available.

clauses.requirement: A creator client keeps exactly one client-local durable transaction per (owner_actor_id, effective_scope, operation=mls_genesis) for a realm or circle scope, never for a sidecar scope, and advances it only along the registered arrows genesis_intent_persisted -> realm_accepted -> governance_result_pinned -> epoch0_state_persisted -> genesis_queued -> genesis_accepted -> artifacts_converged -> ready. The selector is persisted before the first Realm-create side effect, before any governance-evidence read and before any selector-dependent randomness; while the record is still at genesis_intent_persisted the whole closed creation intent MAY be replaced in one atomic durable commit and it is immutable from realm_accepted on; the signed Genesis bytes and the outbound queue item are established atomically; ready and the send-gate index are published atomically. Only an exact accepted Event proves completion, the record never reaches a wire, projection, Account Data key, sync or federation surface, and it never authorizes a peer to trust another party's local state. The accepted Genesis producer explicitly signs creator_leaf_authority binding its sole RFC leaf signature key, endpoint and historical authorization Event; the leaf key need not equal the Event signer key. Before any MLS randomness, governance_result_pinned durably binds the exact accepted scope-create Event and covering Commit, independently verified nonce-bound current authority bundle and complete chain, a verified complete authorized current cut proving exact-scope Genesis absence, complete current creator Actor/device/signer authorization, canonical closed local proposal bytes and digest, and its unchanged governance_binding. Missing, partial, unauthenticated or unavailable reads cannot establish absence or permit generation, upload, signing or enqueue. Existing verified reads supply this evidence; no proof RPC, new wire carrier or Station-signed local proposal is introduced. Every Genesis, including Sidecar, freezes one canonical authoring timestamp into both Event.created_at and payload.created_at. The governing Station rejects inequality with generic failed_precondition before any accepted effect, and consumers independently revalidate this equality before accepting a winner. Proof and commit clocks are independent.

Only MLS ciphersuites registered and active in mls-ciphersuite-registry.json reach the wire. KeyPackage publish, claim and Commit submission each reject an unregistered or inactive ciphersuite; an implementation MUST NOT try several suites in turn until one is accepted, and MUST NOT rewrite a foreign suite identifier into a registered value locally. The recipient endpoint and KeyPackage holder identity is the complete ActorId, and claim, Welcome delivery and leaf credential preserve it verbatim rather than collapsing it to a signing principal, bare DID or handle.

A Commit and all of its Welcome deliveries land in one database transaction: the governance Station verifies the Commit Event, current membership/policy, base group revision and the RFC 9420 public transition, verifies every delivery binding (the claim only for recipients it hosts), appends the RealmCommit, enqueues each hosted recipient's Welcome durably together with that claim's Welcome binding on the claim ledger and writes each cross-Station recipient's Welcome into that routing service's committed-replication outbox intent. Any missing, duplicate, over-limit or mis-bound delivery makes the transaction write nothing, and Commit accepted is returned only after the transaction is durable. The member Station re-verifies a replicated Welcome's claim against its own ledger and queues it, with the same claim-ledger Welcome binding, in the same replica transaction as the Commit replica; a Welcome failing that check is never queued and never blocks the Commit replica. A remote recipient Station separately signs exact accepted Add authority after its existing replica claim check; governance never treats that later proof as a second Commit admission. The own-Station member roster selector binds the authorized accepted target to immutable Genesis provenance without a prejoin client baseline; missing/conflicting authorized provenance fails closed, and ordinary clients independently verify all original signatures and RFC installation.
clauses.test_plan: Audited against the Commit/Welcome transaction contract: a conformance run submits an MlsCommitSubmission whose welcomes[] contains one mis-bound delivery and asserts the Station returns no acceptance and leaves the RealmCommit log, the public group result and every recipient queue unchanged. No vector exists because the obligation is on server transaction atomicity rather than on a byte-level artifact. The historical roster proof read is additionally checked by ak.vector.mls.roster_authority.v1. Member selection additionally requires the roster-client-role carrier vectors and a real authorized since-join replica test without a client Genesis baseline, with wrong Actor/scope/group/target/epoch and missing/conflicting immutable provenance negatives.

clauses.requirement: MLS leaf ownership and Proposal targets preserve the complete ActorId including its Station and never collapse to the signing principal, so remove/update targets match by complete ActorId. There is no exception: no branch matches leaf ownership or a Proposal target by (realm_id, principal_id) alone. Committer authority comes from current capability, membership and policy, never from leaf index, first sender, device presence or UI role.
clauses.test_plan: Audited against the ActorId-completeness rule: a review pass asserts that every MLS leaf, Proposal target and remove/update matching site in the schemas and operation contracts carries a complete ActorId, and that no contract admits a (realm_id, principal_id) matching key. No vector exists because the obligation is on the absence of a reduced matching key.

clauses.requirement: For realm and circle effective scopes the Proposal and Commit wire inputs are complete RFC 9420 PublicMessage MLSMessages, and the governance Station verifies the public transition from the bytes it parsed itself. The membership MAC is verifiable only by a member holding that epoch membership_key, so the Station never obtains member secrets and never treats that MAC as its admission criterion. Shared v1 Commit Events consume inline Proposals only; a referenced Proposal is unsupported_feature with zero writes. The Station freezes, in the accepted Commit transaction, the original zero-based ordinal among all Proposal kinds, exact inline TLS Proposal body, verified full Member sender ActorId and applicable leaf target, then signs that accepted source relation in the roster manifest. A prejoin member need not fetch historically unreadable Commit Events; it verifies the governance manifest, the signed full-record digest, each retained attestor resolution against the original claim receipt and Add attestation historical assertion methods and signatures, and the Add KeyPackage binding, and compares an original Commit only when separately authorized to read it. Remove+Add always creates new provenance even when the leaf tuple is unchanged. Application content and Welcome keep their existing protection, the public handshake discloses nothing beyond the public quantities the section already lists, and a sidecar scope keeps its own separate contract. A Welcome recipient installs a leaf authority map only after a complete signed historical roster is reconstructed from accepted Genesis/Commit provenance and recipient-Station Add attestations; a later-joined member takes immutable Genesis Blob refs from the verified governance-signed roster manifest before the dual-cut authorized self-to-peer material read and derives leaf indices solely from verified RFC public tree bytes. For a Circle scope both cuts use effective Circle membership: the caller's Circle join must still carry the parent Realm member_state current revision as its parent_membership_revision, a target cut at or after the current Circle join is continuous, and an earlier target cut under a Circle join whose bound parent join is no longer current is not_found; Realm and Circle position numbers are never compared. The separate Sidecar contract explicitly uses complete PublicMessage within Sidecar-only disclosure, verifies the actual transition and freezes inline provenance at the exact participant-authority cut, gives MAC verification only to members, and excludes the creator-bootstrap transaction.
clauses.test_plan: Audited against the x-arkret-public-handshake-contract annotation in event-payload.schema.json, which fixes all eight keys this clause states. The review pass asserts the prose and the annotation agree key by key, that no operation accepts a PrivateMessage or standalone bare Proposal handshake input, that no Station-facing schema carries membership_key or any member secret, and that each inline consumed-proposal provenance record comes from the accepted signed Commit bytes. The ak.vector.mls.roster_authority.v1 named fixture tests true wire ordinals across non-Add kinds, referenced-Proposal zero-write refusal, wrong body/sender/ordinal rejection, complete roster, dual-cut disclosure and fail-closed reads. Circle effective-membership and historical-cut continuity are checked by ak.vector.circle.parent_membership_revision.v1. The independent x-arkret-sidecar-handshake-contract is checked by the governance-binding gate with mutations for PrivateMessage, Realm disclosure, Station MAC role and missing exact-cut authority; the Realm/Circle annotation remains scoped to those two kinds.

clauses.requirement: The fixed GroupContext binding is one closed, bounded deterministic-CBOR MlsGroupBinding of five shared members plus participant_authority_digest and authority_stream_head, which the Sidecar scope requires and every other scope MUST omit; authority_stream_head is strictly ascending by UTF-8 bytes and holds at most 64 items: unknown, missing, scope-misplaced, unsorted, indefinite-length, non-minimal, duplicate, out-of-order, trailing, wrong-major-type, out-of-range, invalid-length or resource-limit inputs are rejected. Genesis is 0 -> 0 and a Commit is next_epoch = previous_epoch + 1. Scope, base, epoch and the monotonic unsigned 64-bit key_access_revision counter match the Station current public state and Commit payload field by field, including for otherwise-valid RFC 9420 public material. proposed_group_genesis_binding is not a second binding shape: its formal closed carrier names the ak.mls.genesis route, proposal type, complete sender and target scope, and directly references the same binding schema; any missing required carrier member is rejected as schema_violation before semantic evaluation. Historical accepted material is checked against its historical binding and grants no current send authority. The revision governs key access only and carries no authorization or membership decision of its own.

The Welcome producer proof removes only producer_proof from the closed delivery, recomputes its RFC 8785 JCS SHA-256 digest, signs the registered context-plus-LF and five-member envelope with Ed25519, and is authorized only by the exact winning Commit Event producer method.

Epoch-0 leaf indices are recovered only from the digest-verified RFC 9420 GroupInfo and ratchet_tree extension bytes committed by the accepted genesis, and only from occupied leaves of the verified tree. The consumer hashes the raw bytes against both the explicit digests and the content-addressed refs and validates GroupInfo/tree consistency before use, discarding the whole response on any mismatch. A leaf index is never derived from Add arrival order, Welcome delivery order, roster display order, a recipient list index, an inferred leaf DTO or a proof-bundle leaf, and the provider returns no private tree material, member secret or inferred leaf DTO.
clauses.test_plan: Audited against ak.peer.mls.read.group_state_material.v1, whose contract fixes the all-or-nothing digest verification and the "occupied leaves of the verified RFC tree" derivation rule. The review pass asserts the response schema exposes no leaf DTO, no private tree material and no secret, and that no other registered operation offers a second epoch-0 leaf-index source. No vector exists because the obligation is on the absence of alternative sources.

clauses.requirement: Every peer KeyPackage claim binds the accepted authorization Event id of its closed branch and a destination-signed claim_receipt over the exact claim bytes. On the device branch the requester Station verifies the target device's signed peer directory attestation obtained through ak.peer.keys.read.lookup.v1 with purpose mls_group_admission, requiring its device_authorize_event_id to equal the claim record's and its device_signing_key_did to verify the KeyPackage and LeafNode signatures; the Agent branch keeps its Agent signer evidence rule. The requester completes that check, the claim receipt, the KeyPackage signature and every selector before installing a KeyPackage or authoring a Welcome. The wire carries no PCR, control-history, device or Agent signer-evidence sidecar, and an external verifier never replays PCR genesis, RealmCommits or complete control history.

Before decrypting a producer-signed MlsWelcomeDelivery, the recipient resolves its typed keypackage_claim_ref to the exact durable claim outcome through ak.self.keys.keypackages.read.claim.v1 at its own Account Station, verifies the destination receipt, recomputes the KeyPackage digest and signed LeafNode capabilities, verifies current endpoint authorization and the accepted winning Add Commit on the same Genesis lineage, and compares requester, recipient, KeyPackage, group and epoch bindings. A Welcome Event payload, duplicate claim_ref digest, claim_envelope or embedded claim_receipt MUST NOT be accepted. The original claim is consumed only after new group state is durably stored.

An Applet self Account or managed Ghost joins E2EE through the ordinary device branch rather than a third recipient endpoint branch: its restricted delegated device resolves through an accepted authorization_binding_kind="applet_managed_delegation" ak.device.authorize submitted as an ordinary successor Event in that principal own applet_managed_control PCR. Every KeyPackage publication, Welcome admission and MLS durable receipt from that device is ANDed with the revoke fence of the exact Applet install named by that authorize payload applet_id, failing closed with applet_revoked without waiting for a separate ak.device.revoke.
clauses.test_plan: Audited against the delegation contract: a conformance run fences an Applet install and asserts that the delegated device next KeyPackage publication, Welcome admission and durable receipt are each rejected with applet_revoked while no ak.device.revoke exists and the authorize Event is still present in the PCR, and that historical accepted Events remain verifiable. No vector exists because the obligation is a conjunction across two lifecycles.

clauses.requirement: An ordinary client obtains exact historical signing keys from its own Station using a committed_event_ref copied from an original stream_row or the section 2.1 frozen complete self request Event paired with its bound accepted original Commit consumed from its persistently bound authenticated own Station after Station native governance verification and client exact coordinates/continuity checks. Every result independently keeps the accepted authorization coordinate, revision and governance generation so historical MLS binding remains verifiable; target and authorization refs may differ, and a stable (actor, method, key) triple never substitutes for either exact Event instance. A committed Agent reply with unresolved exact historical signing evidence triggers per-stream resolution independently of product projection changes, later Account frames or a page reload; exact target and producer MLS authorization gates remain mandatory before publishing verified content. Self-submitted Human PCR queries require original same-Station self-admission, exact authenticated recipient/actual producer fullAccount and complete immutable historical authorization/proof; controller Human Agent PCR genesis requires original accepted provision, complete controllerAccount and original delegation in that same transaction. No current-row reconstruction, sibling/foreign source, PCR history permission or floor/head advancement is allowed.
clauses.test_plan: Run ak.vector.signer_key.historical_commit_coordinate.v1 and tools.test_signer_key_historical_coordinate_gate: both historical selectors require the four-coordinate ref, target and authorization remain independent, redacted/current-projection/cursor/time sources stay unresolved, and missing coordinates never downgrade to current query. The fixture is a machine semantic suite; production signer resolution and commit verification remain implementation evidence. Inkson identity::agent_signer_evidence::historical_result_tests::changed_realm_projection_resolves_agent_reply_without_an_account_frame exercises the real HTTP selector and verified producer transition with a changed product projection and no subsequent Account frame. The named suite has no Cotest production executor yet; owner1725 retains live/full-matrix acceptance. The self submission rule mutations cover every source-binding and restricted-PCR field plus each positive/negative flow. Real original admission transaction, key verification, no-history-scan behavior and zero-write denial require native/PG/full evidence in owner1725; these spec fixtures do not establish production correctness.

clauses.requirement: A current self signing-key result serves only the operation that froze it. A same-batch or byte-identical in-flight query may be merged, but a completed result MUST NOT be reused for a future Signal, a future operation or a reconnection. Result association uses complete selector equality rather than array position, and a duplicate, missing or extra selector rejects the whole result.
clauses.test_plan: Audited against signer-key-operations.schema.json and the self query contract: the review pass asserts results carry no reusable lifetime, that the request context is echoed verbatim and bound to the authenticated SessionGrant account, and that association is specified by complete selector equality with no index-based path. No vector exists because the obligation forbids a later reuse rather than fixing a byte artifact.

clauses.requirement: Message prepare distinguishes local plaintext intent from the encrypted wire request: the intent content oneOf is closed, a plaintext prepare is rejected in an MLS-activated scope, and the client freezes its AAD inputs and encrypts locally before calling prepare rather than letting the Station encrypt. The client compares the returned draft ciphertext, encrypted metadata and bindings byte-for-byte against what it froze and fails closed on any difference. An exact retry replays byte-identical bytes, so it never re-encrypts and never consumes another sender ratchet generation. Encrypted prepare and authority-forward submit into a definitely inactive scope return generic failed_precondition without a write; a temporarily unreadable current MLS result returns temporarily_unavailable with exact retry only before a Commit. When the current checkpoint awaits a winning Commit, failed_precondition with epoch_update_required requires the client to pause; when a ready current group differs from the frozen encryption context, top-level epoch_mismatch requires fresh local MLS state and a newly encrypted request. The two-request path assumes send readiness and local MLS state: prepare grants no permission, reserves no sequence, advances no stream position and does not establish MLS state.
clauses.test_plan: Audited against message-authoring.schema.json and operations-error-mapping.json: the review pass asserts message_authoring_content is a closed oneOf of plaintext and mls, that message_prepare_outcome returns only a draft with no acceptance, reservation or position, that epoch_mismatch is registered for prepare and current send admission, and that no prepare request member carries a key or would let the Station encrypt. A conformance run replays a byte-identical prepare and asserts a single ciphertext and no second sender ratchet generation; separate stale-group and pending-Commit cases assert epoch_mismatch versus epoch_update_required and the respective re-encrypt versus pause action. No vector exists because the obligation spans a client-local encryption step the vector harness does not author.

clauses.requirement: ak.capability.relinquish is subject-only self-service: the reducer accepts it only when the acting actor is the grant's own subject, and it MUST NOT additionally require the actor to hold ak.capability.revoke, because a narrow holder would otherwise be unable to give up what it holds. A relinquish by anyone other than the subject is rejected with reason grant_relinquish_not_subject. Descendants of the relinquished grant fail on read through refs, exactly as they do after a revoke.

The personal blocklist is a holder-private whole-value CAS result on one revision counter with a closed target set; shared history and holder-private requests are received before client-side filtering, unblocking rebuilds the projection from retained material, and server submission responses do not reveal blocklist hits. Holder-side automatic receipt differences may reveal filtering and are outside that server guarantee.
Revoking consent immediately invalidates the cached private contact discovery result, the invite capability gate and every scope cache, and the next PSI rotation excludes the peer.

Current peer service authentication precedes idempotency lookup: a revoked origin key yields signature_invalid with zero writes, an active key with a removed origin binding yields capability_denied, and any changed authorization basis requires fresh authorization before an exact cached outcome may replay.

At one accepted authority cut, the ak.invite.claim reducer verifies accepted create Event/Commit, pure lifecycle, effective Realm policy, both proof transcripts, the frozen token commitment and accepted-claim uniqueness. It atomically accepts the exact claim Event/Commit, pending to claimed lifecycle and subject-bound proposal; rejected claims write nothing shared and expiry requires a separate accepted revoke Event.
The third-party claim endpoint and the invite locator resolve endpoint each give every one of their failure classes one external response shape and a bounded, class-independent timing distribution.

An out-of-band invite code below the production entropy floor is refused, and a lookup form exceeding the policy validity window or claim count is invalidated before it can become a pending invite or accepted membership.

Joining a decrypting conference is refused and no media key is published when Realm policy has not authorized media-service decryption, when the SFU service DID is absent from plaintext_visible_services, or when the required plaintext warning was not shown.

The Account Authority issuer ledger chains genesis and CAS successors inside the binding commit transaction, binds each record to its issuer identity and proof, classifies every replica state through one closed table, and bounds the fanout outbox.

clauses.requirement: Published test signing material and reserved test identifiers registered in artifacts/registry/test-material-registry.json MUST be refused on every formal verification, authorization and trust-admission path, independently of whether the signature verifies, because the private key ships with the specification. Matching is by a fingerprint over algorithm-defined public key bytes, so a rename or re-encoding of the same key still matches; the did, key_id and trust_domain reserved-identifier rules are matched independently and by their own typed-identifier semantics, never inferred from the words test, fixture, did:key or example. The refusal is fail-closed with reason test_signing_material_denied, leaves no verified binding, cache entry or accepted auth state, and MUST NOT degrade to a weaker evidence class, a limited_trust pin or a retryable unavailable. Unlisted material is still verified by the ordinary rules, and the isolated conformance harness is the only place the material may execute: the formal API MUST NOT expose a switch onto the test trust path.
Applet Service epoch and each exact Station Account PCR must align native version, document and approved key set; service-first/PCR-first pause business, historical evidence remains immutable.
clauses.test_plan: Contract alignment models pass; independently verify native histories, per-Station CAS, paused business and resumed completion under real Station/runtime restart in owner 0847 before live support.

clauses.requirement: No-URL bootstrap authenticates exact administrator-approved request and Applet epoch possession without active install; submit cannot accept staged facts, terminal CAS and explicit admin commit are durable.

clauses.requirement: Strict invocation uses an independent MLS Circle and exact receiving grants; re-encrypted selected attachments, independently signed plaintext result and current invoker relay cannot transfer original group keys or falsify authorship.
clauses.test_plan: SDK signature and MLS isolation components pass. Live scope/grant/history/blob bypass, revoke, attachment supersets, offline relay and client attribution require independently deployed runtime and clients in 0847. Contract KAT projections are not native authority evidence.

clauses.requirement: Ordinary clients consume only persistently bound authenticated own-Station original governance results, checking full Account and request epoch, exact selectors/scope/cuts, content IDs and per-stream continuity without native method history or retained-signer discovery. Station/auditor governance signature, nonce and native history verification and client producer/MLS/attachment cryptography remain mandatory. No new wire result, operation, boolean trust flag or portable authority is introduced. Successful bound self submit pairs each validated frozen request Event with its original accepted Commit by outcome branch and aggregate slot, constructs only the exact target and advances no timeline head/floor; independent historical producer/MLS verification remains mandatory.
clauses.test_plan: Run the complete official artifact pipeline, including all executable governance_result_consumption_roles fixture policy cases. These cases prove only the machine role/input policy. Audit the authenticated host transport and durable context, then execute native cryptographic negative suites and fresh three-Station S3 bilateral encrypted messages in owner1725; policy fixture success alone is not implementation or live acceptance evidence.

clauses.requirement: An authorized own-Station moderation_franking_proof current row is installed independently of report workflow and moderator verification. The closed selector names the target Event, value repeats that target and Realm, and the value remains the canonical closed FrankingProof. Installing the current row grants no permission or cryptographic verdict; ordinary MLS chat must not wait for a report or optional existence anchor, while invalid source, cut, scope or target bindings fail closed.
clauses.test_plan: Run tools.test_franking_current_installation_gate and the existing franking transcript/controller gates: mutations of selector target type, canonical value reference, row closure and the ordinary-chat independence obligation must fail. This checks schema and normative guards, not moderator verification or native client installation; Inkson current installation and owner1725 live acceptance remain implementation evidence.

clauses.requirement: An explicit original-controller grant to an exact owned Agent needs no general grant action or parent regrant right; both membership generations and ownership are verified, the source is terminal and cannot be reentered by an Agent controller.

All ordinary owned-Agent grant and reading paths remain bounded by current controller authority, original scope, global/key ceilings and shared parent quotas; partial loss, global deny, own-object conditions and equivalent current sources are evaluated without cross-grant splicing.

The default Agent management gate permits member self-service only with verified current absence of restrictions; policy controller selectors cover current and future Agents and user grants or local allow cannot override effective bans. Join-only restrictions preserve existing participation.

The original issuer may revoke its owned-Agent grant with exact CAS without a revoke action or online runtime; ineffective and terminal exact reads remain available, old revoked records never restore and fresh explicitly confirmed grants may be issued under current gates.

Current admission and future reads, subscriptions, attachments and access-material delivery use authoritative controller and management gates; accepted exact retries preserve history and unaccepted candidates revalidate, unknown remote evidence never authorizes new delivery.
